_comment: Diamond, 128-atom supercell, LCAO: density of states and AC conductivity from one setup. Both observables reuse the same S^-1/2 preconditioner and the same Chebyshev machinery, so asking for them together costs one setup instead of two. The velocity the AC task needs is the commutator i[H, r] from the model's dipole integrals, so no pseudopotential files are involved. The 128-atom cell is the primitive cell tiled 4x4x4 at load ('supercell'), with the primitive-cell Hamiltonian folded onto it; the supercell folds the Brillouin zone onto Gamma, which is why one k-point is enough here.

run._comment_conv: The 2s2p1d basis puts core-like states near 250 eV, so the Chebyshev expansion spans ~280 eV. The dos task asks for the resolution directly: dE in eV, with the step and moment counts derived from the span at run time -- cost is linear in span/dE, which is why a wide LCAO span makes fine resolution expensive. nsamples controls the stochastic-trace noise, which shows up as negative excursions in derived quantities like the absorption coefficient if it is too small.
